comment: Grading is very subjective; that said, if you *do the readings* and make an honest effort to participate in class, he will notice and appreciate it. He is very funny and likes to play devil's advocate. Will press your argument and find the weak points. Forces you to think more critically. You will get out of his class what you put into it.

Lopez-Guerra is a unique guy. He proposes lots of debates and conversations, and his teaching style is basically rage baiting you. He has no clear grade guidelines. We weren't given a grade until half way into the semester, and it is 100% subjective. The material is interesting, but it feels like he's improvising the whole time. Take Kielty instead

The only grade in this class is basically a paragraph of critical thinking about the reading and participating in class. He seems intimidating at first, but he mellows out near the end. Participating can be scary, but honestly, if you just ask questions about the reading in class or show some engagement with the content, it's not too hard.

Long, detailed readings. No exams but participation is hefty. Written responses before every class - will cold call to share what you wrote. Can be condescending at times and not super open to feedback/suggestions

do the readings before class and be ready to talk about them. no quizzes, tests, or any long papers at all, for each class theres a reading usually ranging from 20-50pgs sometimes more and need to write a response paper to each one but doesn't need to be long. just participate in class as best you can and he will appreciate it.super funny and smart

Claudio is easily the greatest professor I have ever had in my entire life and this was my favorite class I have ever taken. If you are PPEL, or anything even close to it, you have to take him. The readings can be long and dense but the discussions we have are incredible. I cannot say enough good things about Claudio other than please take him!!

Dr. Lopez-Guerra is a unique professor (in a good way). He's very sharp - he'll routinely play devil's advocate in class just for the heck of it - but doing so makes you think critically and sharpen your perspectives. As long as you do the readings and give them some thought and participate in class, you'll be set. Would reccomend to others.

My favorite professor at UR. I have taken PPEL 262 and PLSC312 with him and would take more if he taught them. Sometimes the readings are a bit dense but he breaks them down in a way that's applicable in our lives and often pretty funny. If you want to participate and challenge your beliefs, he teaches great courses.

Lopez-Guerra is the chillest dude in the PPEL. His class is discussion based, and he expects you to participate and might call you out sometimes but won't do so in a hard way. He's also really understanding and explains things really well, and is clearly passionate about the subject and area field. I would recommend him to any PPEL student.
Analytical response (argument paper) due every class in response to the reading but these are no longer than a page.  Dr. Lopez Guerra has the best seminar classes in all of UR.

Great guy, really smart and funny. He makes every class interesting. Its a lot of work, since you got to do a fairly dense reading and a write-up for every class, but its worth it if you are actually interested.

Professor Lopez-Guerra is one of the funniest professors I have ever had. He is very smart and knows a lot about political philosophy. There are not a lot of grades for the course because the focus is on the readings but I would recommend him to anyone.

Modern Political Theory was one of the best classes I have taken this far. A lot of readings and requires 2 analytical responses before class, but class was discussion based and really interesting. Definetely makes you think critically and improves your analytical skills. Attendance is a big part of your grade so try not to miss many classes.
Great Professor. The class allowed me to improve my writing and critical thinking skills. Absolute must take professor for any PPEL major.

It's an interesting class but definitely more philosophy based. The readings are pretty dense and there are written responses due for every class. The class improves your critical thinking but you definitely have to put time into it.

PPEL 262 was a blast with the number of topics we explored on property rights as Professor Lopez-Guerra broke them down well in class. Readings take time and need to be done every class with a the 1-2 page AR due every class but greatly improves your critical thinking. Overall, enjoyable with the variety of topics explored but challenging.
